newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil vote scandal won't hurt privatization-Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil vote scandal won't hurt privatization-Malan.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan told reporters the cash-for-votes scandal would not undermine the government's privatization drive.
"No, it will not cause any damage," Malan said when asked about the repercussions of the scandal which has rocked the Brazilian Congress since Tuesday.

In a series of reports this week, Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper published telephone conversations between two deputies and an unnamed "Mr X," which suggested Communications Minister Sergio Motta gave them money and a television concession in exchange for their votes.

Motta, who is in charge of the upcoming $35 million privatization of Brazil's telecommunications industry, has denied he was involved in any irregularities in mustering support for a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election.

Malan reaffirmed his position that the best use for the tens of billions of dollars in privatization receipts flowing into government coffers in the next few years would be to pay off debt and thereby reduce debt servicing costs permanently.

He said fiscal accounts were showing an improvement with the consolidated public sector deficit in the 12 months to the end of February 1997 falling to 3.44 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) against more than five percent of GDP in the same period last year.
"This is not a drastic improvement as some had hoped for, but it is an improvement," Malan said. (( -- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
